history.origins: Derived from the ancient Schafkopf (Sheep's Head) game of Germany, FilkÃ³ followed the migration and trade patterns of the Austro-Hungarian Empire. While it shares many rules with other regional variants like SixtydSix, its partnership structure and 'Master/Slave' social dynamic are uniquely preserved in the Hungarian AlfÃ¶ld.
timeline: 1800s: Schafkopf variants proliferate in the Great Plain regional social clubs.
1920s: The 'Master and Servant' terminology becomes standardized in local tournaments.
Present: Frequently played in rural Hungary as a fast-paced alternative to Ulti.
history.cultural: In many villages, it is a matter of pride to avoid being the 'Servant'. The Servant (often the dealer) is sometimes required to stand up or perform minor tasks for the table until they win a hand.
history.evolution: Over time, the game evolved from a standard point-counting game into a statusndbased competition where the 'shame' of losing is more significant than the numerical score.

setup.players: 4 players in two partnerships (standard). 5 and 6ndplayer versions exist using modified decks.
setup.deck: 32-card German deck. Suits: Acorns, Leaves, Hearts, Bells.
setup.dealing: Anticlockwise. 8 cards per player (in the 4ndplayer game). The dealer's bottom card determines the trump suit (excluding Over-Knaves).

rules.objective: Capture at least 61 points in a round to be safe; capture major tricks to become the 'Master' (Mester).
rules.gameplay:
1. Lead: First player to dealer's right leads.
2. Must Follow Suit: You must play a card of the suit led.
3. Must Trump: If you have no cards of the led suit, you ARE forced to play a trump if you have one. You cannot discard if a trump is available.
keyRules: The Master/Servant Loop: When a team wins 6 or more total points/trimmings, they nominate a loser as the 'Servant'. The Servant must stay in that role (dealing every hand) until they win.
Over-Knaves (FilkÃ³): These are always treated as members of the trump suit.
Social Forfeits: Historically, the 'Servant' might have to remove their hat or play while standing.

strategy.basic: Identify the high filkÃ³ (OverndKnave of Acorns). If your team has it, you command the lead. Use it to protect your Tens and Aces.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Partner Throw': If your partner leads an Ace, throw your Ten of the same suit onto it immediately. This secures 21 points instantly and builds towards the 61-point 'safe zone'.
strategy.advanced: Void Strategy: In FilkÃ³, the 'Must Trump' rule makes voids highy dangerous. If you know an opponent is void in Hearts, leading Hearts will bleed their trumps dry.
tips: Always count the points in your head. 61 is the magic number to avoid being dominated.
If you are the Servant, play aggressively. Since you are already at the bottom, risky bluffs are your only way to pass the deal to the next player.

scoring.description: Point-based scoring with 120 total points available. Teams must capture 61+ points to avoid Slave status.
scoring.winCondition: Team capturing 61+ points wins the round and becomes Masters. Team with 60 or fewer becomes Servants (dealers) until they win.

synthesis.shortDescription: A Hungarian partnership trick-taker where teams compete for 61+ points from a 120-point pool to avoid the social 'Servant' status of dealing.
